decisions.reason: The flagship reference electrometer sits at the core of the firm's dosimetry business and is featured on the home page, so dropping it would write off a visible, central commitment.

The risk management software builds on the established offer and fits the announced integration and prediction direction, and its two years of dedicated presentation make any slow adoption easy to attribute to temporary causes.
The CT phantom was launched only recently, builds on the established offer, belongs to the imaging QA push the firm has announced, and costs little to keep.
The mammography phantom is distant from the core and less heavily invested, but it is new and tied to the flagship imaging QA line, so management would likely give it more time.
The full field mammography phantom carries some overlap risk with Product D and low sunk investment, yet the imaging commitment and its recent launch favor keeping it for now.
This multi-model imaging QA line is presented as a flagship of the firm's direction, so heavy investment and public commitment make dropping it very unlikely.
